name: Andy Katz-Mayfield
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Mammoth Brands (formerly Harry's Inc.; owns Harry's, Flamingo, Lume, Mando)
profile: Duke and Stanford GSB (MBA 2011) alum who worked at Bain & Company and Charlesbank Capital before co-founding Harry's with Jeff Raider in 2012. Harry's grew into a ~$750M-revenue DTC/retail razor business; in April 2025 the parent was renamed Mammoth Brands, which he still co-leads with Raider.
interesting_fact: In January 2014, barely a year after launch, Harry's bought the century-old German blade maker Feintechnik (Eisfeld, founded 1920) for $100M so it could control manufacturing; in 2019 Edgewell agreed to buy Harry's for $1.4B before the FTC sued to block it.
deep_cut_fact: His first paying job was as a banquet waiter at a country club, which taught him that great service 'isn't that hard'; he has every Harry's employee spend a day each quarter working in customer experience, and says he wants to build a brand that lasts 100 years.
notes: Co-CEO with Jeff Raider (also Warby Parker co-founder). Best route is Mammoth Brands press email. LinkedIn listed is the company page, not his personal profile.

name: Scott Ringwelski
current_role: Co-founder, Handshake (former CTO; current operating title not publicly stated)
profile: Traverse City, Michigan native and Michigan Tech software-engineering grad ('14) who co-founded Handshake, the college career network, with Garrett Lord and Ben Christensen in 2014 and served as its CTO. Handshake was valued at $3.5B in 2022; Ringwelski keeps a low public profile and is listed today simply as co-founder.
interesting_fact: Handshake was born at a small engineering school in Houghton, Michigan: the founders saw the opportunity gap versus Ivy League students; the platform grew to 18M students and 1,200 schools by 2021.
deep_cut_fact: While Lord and Christensen pitched colleges on the road, he stayed in Houghton building the product; he took the call from Wabash College that became Handshake's first client ('my first and only sales call'), and the first HQ was a rental house with a hole where a basement window should be.
notes: Very low public profile; co-founders call him 'the smartest person in all our CS classes'. Current role unclear (Handshake now lists a different CTO). Route via Handshake press or Michigan Tech alumni network.

name: Tommy Nicholas
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Alloy (identity and fraud-risk decisioning platform for banks and fintechs, New York)
profile: Richmond-raised UVA grad (2011) and self-described software developer who built startups and freelance apps, then ran product at Knox Payments before co-founding Alloy in 2015 with Laura Spiekerman and Charles Hearn. Alloy hit unicorn status in 2021 ($1.55B by 2022) and was on the 2025 Forbes Fintech 50; he still leads it as CEO.
interesting_fact: Alloy sells KYC/AML, fraud and credit-risk decisioning to banks and fintechs; it became a unicorn in October 2021 at $1.35B and in 2024 launched an embedded-finance compliance platform for bank/fintech partnerships.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech he was one of four Richmond locals who built Coffitivity (2013), the viral website that streams coffee-shop ambient noise to boost creativity; he was then a UVA grad working as a developer at Shockoe.com. His first startup, The City Swig (2011), offered real-time nightlife deals in Charlottesville.
notes: Coffitivity link supported by a Richmond Times-Dispatch reprint (names 'Nicholas', UVA grad at Shockoe.com) and his Wikipedia page; mention lightly. Alloy is a fintech, not energy; frequent podcast guest on fraud/AI in banking.

name: Deepak Diwakar
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer, Mindtickle (revenue-enablement software; HQ San Francisco, engineering in Pune)
profile: IIT Bombay computer-science grad (2008) who started as a machine-learning/platform engineer at ad-tech startup PubMatic, then co-founded Mindtickle in Pune in 2011-12 with Krishna Depura, Nishant Mungali and Mohit Garg. Mindtickle became a unicorn in 2021 (~$1.2B) selling sales-readiness and revenue-enablement software; he runs technology and operations as COO.
interesting_fact: Mindtickle helped define the 'sales readiness' software category and was named a Leader in the Forrester Wave for Revenue Enablement Platforms (Q3 2024).
deep_cut_fact: At IIT Bombay he wrote three of the four Performing Arts Festival (PAF) productions during his time there; he is a keen cyclist and nature lover whose mantra is 'Truth, honesty, and transparency build trust, and trust builds transformation.'
notes: Some sources list him as CTO; Mindtickle's own leadership page says COO. Older press releases cite a pr@ Mindtickle mailbox but I could not verify it on a live page, so it is omitted. Recognised by IIT Bombay alumni awards page.

name: Tim Dorr
current_role: Co-founder of Salesloft; Atlanta startup investor/engineer (Techstars Atlanta MD 2022-24, later co-chair; current employer reported inconsistently)
profile: Georgia Tech-rooted Atlanta engineer who co-founded sales-engagement platform Salesloft (2011, with Kyle Porter and Rob Forman) and served as its original technical architect/CTO; Salesloft reached unicorn status and was sold to Vista Equity in 2021. In March 2022 he became Managing Director of Techstars Atlanta (with Cox Enterprises), backing local founders.
interesting_fact: On taking the Techstars Atlanta job he said he wanted to 'pay back into the ecosystem that has gotten me this far' and that he looks for 'the less-than-perfect founder, that 95% founder.'
deep_cut_fact: He is a long-time open-source maintainer of Redux, the JavaScript state-management library used by millions of web apps; his npm handle 'timdorr' sits on the Redux package maintainer list alongside creator Dan Abramov (gaearon) and Mark Erikson.
notes: Current day job unclear: aggregator profiles mention a principal-engineer role at 8th Light (2025) and Techstars Atlanta co-chair; verify before outreach. Very approachable in Atlanta tech circles (ATDC EIR, Atlanta Tech Village advisor). No published email found.

name: Ori Avraham
current_role: Co-founder and VP Product & Strategy, Fabric (formerly CommonSense Robotics; earlier titled CTO)
profile: Israeli Air Force major and Talpiot graduate (physics/maths, Hebrew University; MBA, Tel Aviv University) who co-founded CommonSense Robotics in 2015 with Elram Goren and Shay Cohen. Renamed Fabric in 2019, the company builds robotic micro-fulfillment centers for grocers and retailers and was valued at ~$1B; he now leads product and strategy and holds several patents.
interesting_fact: Fabric's founders came from outside logistics entirely (IDF technology/intelligence backgrounds) and set out to put compact robotic fulfillment centers inside cities so retailers could deliver online orders within an hour.
deep_cut_fact: In the Israeli Air Force he specialised in operations research and received the Air Force Commander Distinction Award; he is a graduate of the elite Talpiot program.
notes: Title varies by source (CTO on Crunchbase; VP Product & Strategy on Fabric's own About page - use the latter). No press email published. Low public profile; Israel-based.

name: Michael Bermingham
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Business Officer, Nium (Singapore cross-border payments; also listed as Global Relationship Officer on some 2025 event pages)
profile: Compliance and FX-industry veteran (Monmouth University BSBA) who spent years at forex broker GAIN Capital, latterly as director of its Australian business, before co-founding remittance startup InstaReM with Prajit Nanu in Singapore in 2014. InstaReM became Nium in 2019, a B2B cross-border payments and card-issuing platform valued at $2B+ in 2021; he drives strategy, partnerships and operations.
interesting_fact: Nium builds all its payments technology in-house and grew from a licensed money-transfer service into a full-stack payments infrastructure provider; in 2020 he said volumes were doubling year on year to about $6B.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech he spent about a decade at GAIN Capital, leading its operations and compliance teams in both the UK and US before running its Australian arm; that regulatory background was the compliance backbone InstaReM was built on.
notes: Goes by 'Mike' on Nium event pages. Low-profile co-founder; Prajit Nanu is the public face. Deep-cut source is an org-chart profile (moderate reliability).

name: Saurabh Saxena
current_role: Founder and CEO, Power Club (formerly Uable, kids' life-skills edtech, Bengaluru); co-founder of Vedantu (exited ~2017-18)
profile: IIT alumnus who co-founded JEE coaching institute Lakshya (2006) with Vamsi Krishna, Pulkit Jain and Anand Prakash; Lakshya was acquired by MT Educare in 2012 and the same team launched live online-tutoring platform Vedantu in 2014, which became a unicorn in 2021. He led academics, left around the 2017 funding crunch, and in 2019 founded Uable, a life-skills platform for 6-16-year-olds, later renamed Power Club.
interesting_fact: Vedantu's name blends the Sanskrit 'Veda' (knowledge) and 'Tantu' (network); it was the founders' second edtech exit-backed venture after selling Lakshya to MT Educare (Zee Learn group) in 2012.
deep_cut_fact: After Vedantu he deliberately moved away from exam prep: his 2019 startup Uable teaches children aged 6-16 life skills such as communication, entrepreneurship and coding through peer communities - a contrast to the IIT-JEE coaching he started his career in.

public_contacts.value: The Desi VC podcast, E119 (guest interview: Saurabh Saxena, co-founder Vedantu, Power Club)

notes: Common name - make sure outreach targets the Vedantu/Uable founder. Exit date reported as 2017 or Jan 2018. No published email found; Power Club website not reachable during research. Podcast entry is an appearance, not his own channel.

name: Markku Koskela
current_role: Co-founder, Oura Health (early CTO / Chief Technology Specialist; current operating role not publicly confirmed)
profile: Oulu, Finland engineer with Nokia/Polar-area R&D background who co-founded Oura Health in 2013 with Petteri Lahtela and Kari Kivela, serving as its technology lead. Oura's sensor ring launched on Kickstarter in 2015, won a CES 2016 Innovation Award and now dominates the US smart-ring market; the company was valued at about $11B after a 2025 Series E.
interesting_fact: Oura is Finland's most valuable startup: 5.5 million rings sold by June 2026, and a 2020 Rockefeller Neuroscience Institute study found the ring could flag COVID-19 about three days before symptoms, leading the NBA and others to adopt it.
notes: Very low public profile; insider listings show his founder/CTO-type role ending around 2020, so he may no longer be operational. Oura's original company name was 'Jouzen'. No sourced deep-cut found (web search budget ran out mid-lane).

name: Thomas Glocer
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Capitolis and BlueVoyant; Chairman, ISTARI; General Partner, Communitas Capital; Lead Director, Morgan Stanley
profile: Former M&A lawyer (Davis Polk, New York/Paris/Tokyo) who joined Reuters' legal team in 1993, became CEO of Reuters Group in 2001 and led the 2008 combination into Thomson Reuters, serving as its CEO until end-2011. Since then he has invested via his family office Angelic Ventures and Communitas Capital and co-founded capital-markets fintech Capitolis (2017) and cyber-defence firm BlueVoyant.
interesting_fact: He went from the Reuters legal department to running the whole company in eight years, becoming Reuters' first American CEO in 2001, and today sits on the boards of Merck, Morgan Stanley (Lead Director) and Publicis Groupe.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond finance he serves on the board of the International Tennis Hall of Fame and the Madison Council of the Library of Congress; in 2017 the Yale Law & Business Society gave him its Annual Alumni Award (he is a Columbia '81 political-science and Yale Law '84 graduate).
notes: Very senior, well-networked; strong fit for data/cyber/fintech topics. 'Reuters first American CEO' widely reported - double-check phrasing before use. Capitolis/BlueVoyant sites blocked automated access so no press emails captured. Ran a personal blog (tomglocer.com) during his CEO years; site currently unreachable.

name: Bolt Ventures
profile: 'Bolt Ventures' is an investment firm, not a person, so this entry looks like a data error in the Hurun unicorn-founder list. Athletic Greens (now AG1) was founded in 2010 by Chris Ashenden, who left in 2024; Kat Cole is now CEO. Bolt Ventures appears to have been listed because it invested in the company, not because it founded it.
interesting_fact: AG1 grew revenue from about $160M in 2021 to about $600M in 2024, largely through podcast advertising; Tim Ferriss was an early promoter and later an investor.
notes: Not a person, so there is nothing to profile. If the journalist wants AG1, the relevant people are current CEO Kat Cole or founder Chris Ashenden (who resigned in 2024 after past convictions became public; that history is not suitable outreach material). I did not confirm Bolt Ventures' exact role in AG1's funding.

name: Carolyn Childers
current_role: Co-founder, Chief (private network for senior women executives); stepped back from the CEO role when Alison Moore was appointed CEO in January 2025 (current title not confirmed)
profile: Former Handy and Primary Venture Partners executive who co-founded Chief in New York in January 2019 with ex-Casper VP Lindsay Kaplan. Chief grew from 400 members to 20,000+, became a $1.1B unicorn in 2022 after a $100M CapitalG-led round, and runs clubhouses in New York, Chicago, San Francisco and Washington DC. In 2025 the founders handed the CEO role to Alison Moore.
interesting_fact: Chief grew from 400 members in March 2019 to 20,000 senior women leaders by October 2022; about 70% of members had their membership paid by their employers, and speakers have included Michelle Obama and Indra Nooyi.
deep_cut_fact: Before Chief she worked at venture firm Primary Venture Partners, which then backed Chief as an early investor alongside General Catalyst chairman Ken Chenault, who joined Chief's board. She told Chief's founding story on Masters of Scale in April 2022 ('How Chief became a phenomenon').
notes: Her role since the January 2025 CEO transition is not stated in the sources I could access; check before outreach. The deep-cut Primary link combines two Wikipedia statements (her former employer, and Primary as an early investor).

name: Ignacio Bachiller
current_role: Co-founder and co-leader (CEO), Fever, the live-entertainment discovery and ticketing platform (New York/Madrid)
profile: Spanish entrepreneur who has co-led Fever with Francisco Hein and Alexandre Perez since its 2014 product launch; the company started in Barcelona in 2012. Fever grew into a global live-entertainment platform (Candlelight concerts, immersive exhibitions, ticketing for FC Barcelona, Formula 1 and X Games), bought London's DICE in 2025 and raised a record $250M led by EQT. It operates in 55+ countries.
interesting_fact: Fever says it reached more than 300 million people in 55+ countries last year. Formula 1 picked it to run F1.com race ticketing from 2027, and it pitches itself as infrastructure for 'what AI cannot replace: the energy of a live crowd.'
notes: Fever's newsroom also lists named regional press officers; use press@feverup.com first. No sourced personal deep-cut found because the web search budget ran out during this lane.

name: Sagi Gidali
current_role: Co-founder of Perimeter 81 (acquired by Check Point in 2023, now 'Harmony SASE'); current role not confirmed
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur who with Amit Bareket first built consumer VPN SaferVPN (sold to J2 Global), then reused its six-year-old network infrastructure to found zero-trust network-security company Perimeter 81 in Tel Aviv in 2018. Perimeter 81 hit a $1B valuation in a 2022 Series C led by B Capital and was bought by Check Point for $490M in 2023.
interesting_fact: Perimeter 81 went from a $100M valuation to unicorn status in about two years (2020-2022), with 2,500+ customers including Fortune 500 firms; Check Point rebranded it Harmony SASE after buying it.
deep_cut_fact: Perimeter 81 was not built from scratch: its first product ran on the global network that Gidali and Bareket had spent about six years building for their earlier consumer company, SaferVPN.
notes: Long-time partner of Amit Bareket. I could not confirm his post-acquisition role (Check Point or a new venture), and found no published contact; LinkedIn is likely the best route. The deep-cut is company history, not a personal detail.

name: Sebastien Cross
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Innovation Officer, BeZero Carbon (London carbon-credit ratings agency)
profile: UK economist who started his career at the Bank of England and then did fixed-income research at Bank of America, before co-founding BeZero Carbon with CEO Tommy Ricketts in 2020. BeZero publishes credit-rating-style quality ratings for carbon-offset projects, bringing capital-markets research methods to the voluntary carbon market. As CIO he focuses on regulation, market structure and product.
interesting_fact: BeZero applies a bond-market idea to climate: like an S&P or Moody's for carbon credits, it rates how likely each offset is to deliver the tonne of CO2 reduction it claims.
deep_cut_fact: Before carbon markets he was an economist at the Bank of England, where he began his career; he holds a BA in Economics from the University of Sheffield and an MSc in Finance & Economics from Warwick Business School.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/climate podcast (carbon-market integrity, regulation). Goes by 'Seb'. Company valuation per Hurun ~$1B; I did not verify it independently.

name: Pau Ramon
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Factorial (Barcelona HR, payroll and business-management software)
profile: Barcelona software engineer who co-founded Factorial in 2016 with Jordi Romero (CEO) and Bernat Farrero. Factorial sells all-in-one HR and operations software to SMEs, became a unicorn in 2022 and has since raised at a reported $2.5B valuation; Ramon leads engineering as CTO.
interesting_fact: Factorial is one of Spain's few software unicorns and is now valued at $2.5B, built on the idea that small and mid-sized companies need the HR, time-tracking and payroll tools that only big companies used to have.
deep_cut_fact: He is a long-time open-source JavaScript developer (handle 'masylum'): he wrote the early Node.js MongoDB library 'mongolia', maintained the 'connect-mongodb' session store, and created 'mobx-rest', and Factorial's own front-end libraries are published on npm under his account.
notes: Engineer-founder with a low media profile; Jordi Romero is the public face. 'Masylum' handle confirmed via npm package metadata naming Pau Ramon. I deliberately left out the developer email that appears in old package metadata.

name: Krunal Desai
current_role: Co-founder, First Mode (company's assets sold to Cummins in Feb 2025); current role unknown
profile: Engineer listed among the 11 former Planetary Resources (asteroid-mining startup) staff who founded First Mode near Seattle in March 2018. First Mode pivoted from space engineering to decarbonizing heavy industry, building hybrid battery and hydrogen fuel-cell powertrains for mining haul trucks and rail, and became valuable mainly through its Anglo American partnership. Cummins bought its hybrid mining and rail business in February 2025.
interesting_fact: With Anglo American, First Mode built what was billed as the world's largest hydrogen-powered mine haul truck, a converted Komatsu 930E unveiled in 2022 at the Mogalakwena platinum mine in South Africa.
deep_cut_fact: First Mode's founding team came straight out of asteroid mining: all 11 founders were former Planetary Resources staff who turned spacecraft-engineering skills toward decarbonizing terrestrial mining.
notes: Identity marked uncertain: Wikipedia lists him as a founder but I could not confirm his background or role (search budget ran out, and firstmode.com now redirects to Cummins). First Mode filed for Chapter 11 in Dec 2024 before the Cummins asset sale, so the Hurun '$2B' valuation is outdated. Avoid that topic in outreach. Strong energy-transition fit.

name: Jia Jianxu
current_role: Director, President and Deputy Party Secretary, SAIC Motor (majority owner, ~54%, of IM Motors / Zhiji)
profile: Chinese state-owned-enterprise auto executive (born February 1978, MBA) who rose through SAIC's parts arm Yanfeng (seating and interiors), SAIC's European and Hong Kong units and then ran SAIC Volkswagen, before becoming president of SAIC Motor. IM Motors is SAIC's premium-EV joint venture with Alibaba and Zhangjiang Hi-Tech (founded December 2020). He is a corporate executive rather than an equity founder.
interesting_fact: IM Motors, the SAIC-Alibaba-Zhangjiang EV joint venture, went from 5,000 sales in 2022 to about 81,000 in 2025 and raised over RMB 8B in a 2024 Series B led by Bank of China Asset Management.
deep_cut_fact: Before running carmakers he spent years in auto parts: he was deputy GM and executive deputy GM of Shanghai Yanfeng Johnson Controls Seating, then general manager of Yanfeng Automotive Trim Systems, and he also served abroad as deputy GM of SAIC Luxembourg and SAIC Europe.
notes: Hurun's 'founder' label is misleading: he is a state-owned-enterprise executive with no personal founder equity confirmed. I could not confirm his formal IM Motors title (IM's public co-CEO is Liu Tao). Outreach would go through SAIC corporate communications and is unlikely to work for a Western podcast.

name: Chris Bisnett
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Huntress (managed endpoint detection and response for SMBs and MSPs; Columbia, Maryland); also on the board
profile: Former NSA cyber operator who co-founded Huntress in 2015 with Kyle Hanslovan (CEO) and John Ferrell, after the core technology began at their defense-contracting firm StrategicIO. Huntress sells managed threat detection and response to small and mid-sized businesses through managed service providers, and passed a $1.5B valuation with a $150M Series D in 2024 (Kleiner Perkins, Meritech). He leads its technology as CTO.
interesting_fact: Huntress began with a $50,000 seed check from Virginia's Mach37 cybersecurity accelerator in late 2015 and grew into a unicorn that protects small businesses that can't afford their own security teams.
deep_cut_fact: Before Huntress was a product, its threat-hunting technology was developed inside StrategicIO, the small defense-contracting shop he and his co-founders ran after leaving NSA offensive cyber operations.

public_contacts.value: https://www.huntress.com/contact-us (press page directs media inquiries here)

notes: CEO Kyle Hanslovan is the company's public voice; Bisnett is more technical. Wikipedia notes a June 2026 employee-conduct allegation at the company. Don't raise it in outreach.

name: Gong Jianjun
current_role: Listed by Hurun as founder of Cowell Health (高济健康 / Gaoji Health); role not verified
profile: Hurun's unicorn list names him as founder of Cowell Health, valued at about $1B. Cowell Health's website (cowellhealth.com) is branded 高济 (Gaoji), a Chinese retail-pharmacy and pharmaceutical e-commerce platform run by a Beijing operator. I could not independently confirm his biography or title.
notes: Minimal record. The web search budget ran out, and Baidu Baike and Wikipedia gave no usable data, so I could not verify identity or details. Chinese-language research (e.g. 龚建军 高济健康) is needed before any outreach. 'Gong Jianjun' is a common name.
